problem_text:
A logistics coordinator needs to assign shipments to identical cargo planes. Shipments:
* Shipment Alpha: volume 41 cubic meters
* Shipment Beta: volume 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Gamma: volume 55 cubic meters
* Shipment Delta: volume 48 cubic meters
* Shipment Epsilon: volume 52 cubic meters
* Shipment Zeta: volume 58 cubic meters
* Shipment Eta: volume 60 cubic meters
* Shipment Theta: volume 56 cubic meters
* Shipment Iota: volume 41 cubic meters
* Shipment Kappa: volume 68 cubic meters
* Shipment Lambda: volume 59 cubic meters
* Shipment Mu: volume 43 cubic meters
* Shipment Nu: volume 46 cubic meters
* Shipment Xi: volume 56 cubic meters
* Shipment Omicron: volume 57 cubic meters
* Shipment Pi: volume 61 cubic meters
* Shipment Rho: volume 33 cubic meters
* Shipment Sigma: volume 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Tau: volume 61 cubic meters
* Shipment Upsilon: volume 51 cubic meters
* Shipment Phi: volume 70 cubic meters
* Shipment Chi: volume 33 cubic meters
* Shipment Psi: volume 50 cubic meters
* Shipment Omega: volume 61 cubic meters
* Shipment A1: volume 53 cubic meters
* Shipment B1: volume 70 cubic meters
* Shipment C1: volume 58 cubic meters
* Shipment D1: volume 34 cubic meters
* Shipment E1: volume 35 cubic meters
* Shipment F1: volume 64 cubic meters
* Shipment G1: volume 48 cubic meters
* Shipment H1: volume 48 cubic meters
* Shipment I1: volume 69 cubic meters
* Shipment J1: volume 57 cubic meters
* Shipment K1: volume 51 cubic meters
* Shipment L1: volume 59 cubic meters
* Shipment M1: volume 37 cubic meters

Each cargo plane can carry up to 100 cubic meters of volume. Assign all shipments using the fewest planes. Each shipment must be loaded onto exactly one plane, and the total volume on a plane cannot exceed its capacity.
